judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite dispute mechanism with a stated notice period; nothing lexically two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 9.4's grant of exclusive Bankruptcy Court jurisdiction, but is limited to Trustee/Committee disputes while 9.4 reaches holders and 'any other party in interest' — a gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Holder access turns on 'purposes reasonably related to such holder's interests', 'undue burden' and 'not detrimental to the Liquidating Trust' — three open-ended gatekeeping standards controlled by the Trustee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives holders something 2.3 says they do not have (rights in administration), though information rights and administration rights are distinguishable; otherwise consistent with 6.2 reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without prior or further authorization' is unqualified language stacked between two 'except' clauses, making the sentence hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read alone it contradicts 3.3(e)'s Committee-approval requirement for dispositions of $5,000 or more; only the opening 'except as otherwise set forth in this Trust Agreement' saves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within a reasonable time after liquidation of all assets' is a vague deadline, and the Class 1 sentence appears without any definition or context in this agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Trust is repeatedly said to exist solely for allowed Class 2 claims (recitals, 1.1(a), 2.1), yet this operative clause directs distributions to Class 1 secured claimants; the section number 3.7 is also skipped.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parentheses are unbalanced — '(including the receipt ... Internal Revenue Service) upon audit if not contested by the Trustee)' — so the qualifier's scope is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is numbered 3.8 while a second, different section is also numbered 3.8 (Compliance with Laws), and no 3.7 exists, leaving cross-references indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, plain catch-all filing duty; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2(g) and 6.1-6.2; it shares the duplicated 3.8 numbering problem only derivatively.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite as a compliance covenant, though 'proceeds of borrowings, if any' assumes a borrowing power the clause does not describe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears the same section number 3.8 as the reporting section, and no provision of this agreement authorises borrowing even though 4.7(b) also assumes borrowing 'in accordance with the terms of this Trust Agreement'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As permitted by herein' is ungrammatical, and 'except that the Trustee may deal with the Trust Assets as permitted by herein' undercuts the 'solely in a fiduciary capacity and not otherwise' rule it follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 3.2's broad grant and 3.3(b)'s no-commingling rule the exception is probably harmless, but its relationship to the fiduciary standard in 4.3(a) is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable business judgment' and 'expeditious but orderly' are soft standards, and clause (a) covers suits 'whether or not such suits are brought in the name of ... the Debtor', which raises a capacity question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates 3.1 and overlaps 3.2, and its power to prosecute 'all claims, rights and rights of action transferred, or assigned or contributed' begs the 1.1(a) question of what was actually transferred.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional exculpation carved back for 'willful misconduct, gross negligence or fraud'; the terms are familiar and reasonably determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same triad appears in 4.3(c), 4.3(d), 4.7(a) and 5.2's definition of Cause, so the instrument is internally consistent on the standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence — 'their determinations shall not result in the imposition of liability upon the Trustee' — is awkward but its protective sense is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the counsel-reliance sentence in 4.4 without contradicting it; both sit under the 4.3(a) standard of care.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad indemnity for 'all liabilities, losses, damages, claims, costs and expenses ... arising out of or due to their actions or omissions', qualified by a clear proviso; the catch-all is wide but the exception is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 4.3(f) (indemnity only to the extent not insured) and 4.3(d) (advancement with repayment) — carve-outs rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The repayment obligation is imposed only on 'the Trustee' although advances may go to the Committee or its members, an asymmetry visible on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 4.3(c) and 4.3(f), it is unclear whether advances are also limited to uninsured amounts; that is a genuine, if small, unresolved interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Remain available to and be binding on' a former or deceased Trustee is a compressed phrase, but its survival purpose is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.3-5.4 on successor trustees; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, clear condition: indemnity only to the extent not covered by insurance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies 4.3(c)'s broader indemnity and presupposes the optional insurance in 3.2(m); the interaction is a deliberate carve-out, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard reliance protection; 'no reason to believe to be other than genuine' is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps 4.3(b) on counsel reliance without contradicting it; consistent with 4.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In the absence of actual knowledge to the contrary' is a clear condition, and the protection is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It protects third parties who do not inquire into authority even where 3.3(e) required Committee approval for a $5,000-plus sale — a real interaction a court might have to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated (a)-(c) investment list with an express expansion/contraction mechanism tied to the tax rules; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the cross-reference in 3.2(s) and the tax-status limits in 3.3(a); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Trustee and shall be entitled to reimbursement' is a mechanical error, and the fee-increase sentence — unlimited in amount, 'no more than once per calendar year', 'without approval of the Bankruptcy Court' — is one-sided and open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 3.3(d), which limits compensation 'to the extent, and in the manner provided in, the Plan', and against 9.8's rule that the Plan controls; the unilateral raise power is hard to reconcile with those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is conditional and readable, but it turns on the Trustee being 'unable to borrow funds ... in accordance with the terms of this Trust Agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision of this agreement grants any borrowing power (3.2's enumerated powers omit it), so the condition references terms that do not exist, as does 3.8's mention of 'proceeds of borrowings'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five words with one meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere requires a bond; 9.8's Plan-control rule is the only conceivable qualifier.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The temporal phrase is garbled — 'while serving as Trustee under this Trust Agreement following the termination of this Trust Agreement or following the earlier of his or her removal or resignation' — so the period covered by the duty is genuinely unclear, and 'earlier of' has only one listed alternative pair.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else addresses trustee confidentiality; 3.4's confidentiality agreements run the other way (holders to Trustee), so no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final relative clause — 'an earlier effective date, which shall be the date that appointment of a successor Trustee becomes effective' — has an uncertain antecedent and appears to contradict the 90-day notice it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 5.2 (Committee may remove and replace) and 5.4, it is not clear whether resignation is effective before a successor is appointed; the appointment power here rests with the court, while 5.2 gives replacement to the Committee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Cause' is carefully defined for court removal, yet the next sentence lets the Committee remove 'without cause', which makes the definition largely superfluous; 'unresolved material conflict of interest' is also vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 5.1, where the Bankruptcy Court appoints a successor on resignation, and 3.3(e)'s supervisory scheme; who controls trusteeship is left with two different answers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary succession mechanics; 'in form satisfactory to the successor Trustee' is odd (the successor approves its own instrument) but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4; no contrary provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but specific; the enumerated (i)-(iii) transition duties and the power-of-attorney are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 5.1-5.3 and 4.3(e)'s survival provision; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If applicable' at the end of the 1145 sentence is loosely placed, and the compliance duty is conditioned on the Trustee's own determination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates the Trust having to comply with the Investment Company Act, whereas 3.3(c) forbids any action that would make the Trust subject to that Act — the clearest internal tension in Article 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Technical but carefully specified allocation mechanics with a stated valuation convention.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.8(a)'s grantor-trust filing position and the recitals' tax-status objective; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terminate on the earlier of' completion and the fifth anniversary 'unless extended' is internally awkward, and 'if any Trust Assets are not duly claimed' introduces an undefined notion of claiming.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The three-year extension cap and 'without further order of the Bankruptcy Court' interact with 9.8 (Plan controls) and 8.1 (amendments must not prolong the Trust); the sentence also assumes distributions 'prior to and upon termination' that 3.6 defers until all assets are liquidated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any substantive provision ... may be amended or waived' invites the expressio unius inference that non-substantive provisions may be changed some other way, and 'substantive' is itself undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 9.1, which allows retroactive amendment to comply with tax law, and 9.8, which subordinates this agreement to the Plan; whether the Trustee and Committee can amend against Plan terms is unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is itself an interpretive rule ('any ambiguity herein shall be construed consistent herewith') and authorises retroactive amendments — language whose reach a party would test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It competes with 9.8's rule that the Plan controls and with 8.1's amendment procedure requiring Committee approval, since 9.1 speaks of amendment without naming who consents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear vesting of privileges plus an unqualified 'sole discretion' to waive, which is broad but unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2(j); the only tension is with 4.1's insistence that powers be exercised 'solely in a fiduciary capacity'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard further-assurances plus an express waiver of reversionary interests; 'necessary or proper' is a familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces 1.1(a) and 1.1(c); 'all of its books and records' is unqualified but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two governing bodies of law are stacked ('California law ... and federal bankruptcy law to the extent applicable') and exclusive jurisdiction lasts only 'for so long as the Chapter 11 Case may be pending', leaving the post-closing forum unaddressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 3.3(g)'s Bankruptcy Court dispute procedure, but the temporal limit means disputes could be litigated elsewhere while other provisions assume continuing court supervision (7.1, 5.1).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate severability with conventional wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the instrument cuts against it; 9.8's Plan-control rule operates independently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice is 'deemed to have been sufficiently given' only if deposited in the mail, with no provision for email or personal delivery, and no address is given for the Debtor or the Committee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(f) expressly permits Committee notices and approvals by email, and 4.7(a) requires mailed notice of fee increases; the mail-only formula does not cover the whole instrument's notice practice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings clause with a single meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters mainly because 1.1's heading ('Assignment and Assumption of Claims') promises more than its text delivers, which this clause tells a court to disregard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Incorporates the provisions of the Plan' is broad and undifferentiated, and 'found to be inconsistent' does not say by whom or on what standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the instrument's conflict rule, and there are provisions it must resolve — 3.6's Class 1 distributions, 1.2's Class 3 reference, 4.7(a)'s fee increases against 3.3(d) — so its operation is likely to be tested.
